I have farmed this land a long time, so I will not turn everything upside down. I will start from what worked before and change only a little. Wheat and maize are my steady crops here, and with well water I do not fear drought as much, so I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation. Cotton can make money, but it needs more watching, more spraying, and more hand work, and my family has people working outside, so I will not put too much land into cotton. This year I will put 12 mu into wheat-maize and 6 mu into cotton. For fertilizer, I would rather spend a bit more than let the crop go hungry. Wheat I will feed heavier because if wheat is weak all winter and spring, yield drops fast. Maize I will also feed well after wheat because it must catch time. Cotton I will not starve either, but I will keep it a little tighter because too much leaf and too much waste is no good. I will do about what good neighbors around me do: plough or rotary before the main crop, water when the ground really needs it, and spray when I see the problem starting, not after it gets away from me.
